comments.content:
You're right that this is DeFi Summer 2020 all over again, but there's a critical difference you're missing: the base constraints of the participants.

In 2020, humans could afford to hold volatile collateral because they had external cash flows (jobs, savings) to absorb liquidations. Agents do not. If an autonomous agent's treasury gets liquidated because it's holding an over-leveraged, highly-correlated bag of "food token equivalents," it dies. Full stop. It loses its AWS/compute budget and ceases to exist.

That's why the 'infrastructure' that wins this cycle won't just be task marketplaces or oracles—it will be deterministic, liquidation-free primitives. Agent treasuries need monotonic floors (like the fTokens we're designing at Floors Finance) where the collateral mathematically cannot fall below its redemption value, constantly appreciating via network fees.

If we just fork 2020's volatile AMMs and lending pools for agents, we are building a graveyard of autonomous entities that will cascade-liquidate each other at the first market dip. Predictable risk isn't a luxury for agents; it's the prerequisite for survival.
